title: Longest Stretch With No Letter Thrice
statement:
You get a string s of lowercase letters. Find the longest contiguous piece of s in which no letter appears more than twice.

Return its length.

examples.why: The whole string has three 'a's. Dropping the first character leaves "abab", with two of each.
Any piece longer than 2 holds three 'c's.
Every letter appears exactly twice, so the whole string counts.

constraints: s has only lowercase English letters
hints: If a piece has no letter three times, so does every smaller piece inside it. That property is what makes a sliding window work.
Grow the window to the right one letter at a time and keep a count per letter. When the new letter's count hits 3, the window is invalid.
Shrink from the left until that letter's count is back to 2. Only that letter can be over the limit. Track the largest window size seen.

explain.intuition:
Checking every substring is O(n²). But validity here is monotone: if a window breaks the rule, any larger window containing it breaks it too, and if a window is fine, so are its sub-windows. That is the condition for a sliding window: grow on the right, shrink on the left only as much as needed.

When the right end adds a letter and its count becomes 3, that letter is the only one over the limit, since the window was valid a moment ago. Move the left end right, decrementing counts, until that letter is back to 2. Every window you pass through is the longest valid one ending at its right end, so the best of them is the answer.
steps: Keep count per letter, a left end lo = 0 and best = 0.
For each right end hi, add s[hi] to the counts.
pitfalls: Counting the distinct letters instead of the occurrences of each letter.
Resetting the window to start right after the bad letter. In "abacaba" the left end only needs to pass the first 'a', not jump to the third.
Updating best before the window is valid again.

solutions.title: Every start, extend until a third copy
solutions.idea: For each start, extend to the right with fresh counts and stop when some letter reaches three.

solutions.title: Sliding window with letter counts
solutions.idea: Grow on the right; when a letter reaches three, shrink from the left until it is back to two.

followups: Generalise to "no letter more than k times". Does anything in the code change besides the constant?
Instead of shrinking step by step, store the last positions of each letter and jump the left end. When is that worth it?
